For any caller and any nonzero, nonzero-address receiver/amount, when the owner calls sendTo with value X the call either succeeds and reduces contract balance by X (reference always reverts on failures so either sent or reverted) — specifically: when receiver's fallback reverts, the reference C's transfer will revert the whole call (so no balance change) while the mutant using call returns false and may not revert, breaking the rule that sendTo always reverts on a failing callee; thus for some receiver that reverts the mutant allows completion vs reference reverting.

For any caller and any nonzero receiver/amount where the caller is the owner, C.sendTo either succeeds only when the external transfer to the receiver does not revert; i.e., calls to sendTo to a receiver whose fallback/receive ALWAYS reverts will always revert on the reference but may succeed on the mutant that uses low-level call and checks the boolean, so the mutant can return (not revert) while the reference reverts.

For any nonzero amount and nonzero receiver address passed by the owner, calling sendTo reverts when the receiver's fallback always reverts; the reference (using transfer) always reverts in that case, while the mutant (using call) can complete (not revert) enabling a difference.

For every receiver contract that always reverts on receiving ETH, a call to C.sendTo by the owner must revert (reference uses transfer so it always reverts), whereas the mutant using low-level .call may return success=false and (if not handled properly) allow the call to complete or behave differently — so the general rule: owner-invoked sendTo to a reverting receiver always reverts in the reference but not necessarily in the mutant.

For any nonzero amount and nonzero receiver address provided by the owner, calling sendTo reverts when the receiver's fallback/receive always reverts (reference using transfer reverts on such failing recipients; the mutant using low-level call can return success=false and allow completion), so the reference always reverts while the buggy mutant can complete successfully for some adversarial receiver.
